title: 6 Undead + Dragon / Harpy

sources.label: HOW TO PLAY The Strongest 6 Undead Build In Auto Chess

body:
# 6 Undead + Dragon / Harpy

The strongest board in the game, and also the hardest to pilot. The Undead
species trait plagues *both* teams — at 6 Undead, every non-undead piece loses
40% max health. Halving the enemy's effective HP means your casters delete them,
and Wraith King revives your own dead for a second fight, so once the snowball
starts you are nearly unkillable in the ultra-late game. The catch is the setup:
it depends on a round-3 neutral item and on winning early, and if you can't win,
the whole engine stalls.

## The Ascetics Cap engine

Everything starts with the **Ascetics Cap** (a tier-2 neutral item you want by
round 3). Put it on a unit; if that unit **wins the round and survives**, it dies
and is reborn next round as a rendered **Undead** unit — provided the piece is
level 5 or below. The hidden tech: a *two-star* tier-3 unit (like a two-star
Treant Protector) is still "level 5", so you can cap a cheap two-star and get a
**two-star** undead back. This is how you assemble six different undead quickly
and cheaply. You must keep a bench slot open for the reborn unit.

## Core Units

Six *different* undead is the first big power spike. The legendary undead are the
payoff; the cheap undead round out the count.

| Unit | Cost | Tags |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lich | 4 | Mage, Undead (primary caster) |
| Necrophos | 5 | Undead, Warlock (primary nuke) |
| Wraith King | 5 | Undead, Warrior (team revive) |
| Spectres | 5 | Demon Hunter, Undead (damage) |
| Vengeful Spirit | 2 | Demon Hunter, Harpy, Undead |
| Winter Wyvern | 1 | Dragon, Mage, Undead |
| Dragon Knight | 4 | Dragon, Human, Knight |
| Jakiro | 5 | Dragon, Mage |
| Skywrath Mage | 1 | Harpy, Mage (2nd harpy) |
| Pudge | 3 | Undead, Warrior (front) |

Two synergies bolt on cleanly. **3 Dragons** (Winter Wyvern, Dragon Knight,
Jakiro) grant 100 starting mana so Lich and Necrophos cast almost instantly.
**2 Harpies** (Vengeful Spirit + Skywrath Mage) add +1 target to single-target
spells — turning Necrophos's ult and Lich's chain into multi-kills.

## Items

- **Spell Prism** on both Lich and Necrophos — the standout undead item, adding
  +1 target to their single-target nukes (stacks with Harpy).
- **Refresher Orb** on Necrophos to double-cast.
- **Manta Style** on Spectre; **Assault Cuirass** on Wraith King for team armour.
- **Gleipnir** to root clustered enemies, and **Guardian Greaves** for sustain.

## Leveling / Roll Plan

Win early, greed levels (even to 6) to keep winning and keep capping units into
undead. Level hard to 8/9 to start finding legendaries, and push level 11+ for
the fuller synergy stacks. If you **can't** win the early game, the fallback is a
Priest lose streak — keep Shadow Demon and Undying (a Priest and Undead) on
board, survive on tangoes, and rebuild the undead count from round 15 onward.
That path is far weaker and much later, but it survives.

## Positioning / Matchup Notes

Keep the capped unit protected (a corner) so it survives to convert. Cluster your
legendaries near a two-star Wraith King so his revive reaches them, and put Lich
in a corner so smoke/silence effects don't cancel his balls. Do **not** go 9
Undead — the third tier's health drain is negligible and dilutes your board. The
build's natural predators are three-star Riki (smoke cloud silences your casters
— answer with Gleipnir roots) and three-star Phantom Assassin / Faceless Void
assassin bursts (spread and pray). Bringing a Pandaren with Lucky Fish early is
the highest-roll opener — it can hand you a free legendary undead like Wraith
King on round 5.
